sharedAssociations.basis: Both imported entries identify the Apalachee people of the Florida panhandle; discontinuous map coverage is distinct from community history.

scopeNotes: The Apalachees entry spans 1492 to 1500 and the Apalachee entry 1530 to 1650. Both name the same Florida people in nearby approximate imported polygons, so they share a narrative. No claim of identical borders or continuous map coverage is made.
A culture classification distinguishes a continuing people from a single fixed state. It does not deny Apalachee chiefly institutions or imply the absence of political organization.
Lake Jackson site dates are not an ethnic founding date. Fort Walton is an archaeological classification, not a separate kingdom automatically interchangeable with every historic Apalachee community.

The Martin-site pig’s nineteenth-century date supersedes the older de Soto interpretation. Conflicting numerical calibration statements on the source page are not reproduced. Burned clay alone does not identify who burned a building.
San Luis visitor buildings are modern reconstructions. Ancient dimensions and uses are distinguished from modern construction methods.

Mission documents describe colonial institutions and outsider interpretations. The ballgame manuscript is cited through the museum timeline, not represented as an original manuscript personally examined.
The Northwestern State University account synthesizes archival research. The original petitions and land records were not separately inspected; precise allegations are attributed to those records.
Mobile is named without the historical administrative label French Louisiana, to avoid confusing its location with the modern state of Louisiana.

Present community organizations are distinguished without adjudicating leadership, membership, trademarks or federal and state recognition. Introduced legislative resolutions were not used as proof of enacted legal status.

No conquest successor is linked because no single territorial transfer with a verified runtime target has been established. Independent historical review, geometry assessment and depth certification remain pending.
